neighbours.label: the comma or 'as' right after a health or safety instruction, where a reason clause ('because', 'as', 'even if') follows
fire: If you start to feel dizzy during the workout, stop at once, because overheating can be dangerous.
Do not mix bleach with other cleaners, as the fumes can damage your lungs.
Avoid heavy meals late in the evening, because they make it harder to fall asleep.
Place a carbon monoxide alarm near every bedroom, as the gas has no smell.
Take the full course of antibiotics, even if you feel better after a few days.
Never leave a toddler alone near a pool, because drowning happens silently.
Wear sunscreen on cloudy days too, as ultraviolet light passes through clouds.
Limit salty snacks, because too much sodium raises blood pressure.
quiet: When she started to feel dizzy during the workout, she sat down and drank some water.
My grandmother mixed bleach with water to clean the kitchen floor every Sunday.
We had a heavy meal late in the evening and then walked along the river.
The landlord placed a new alarm near every bedroom last spring.
He took the full course of antibiotics and went back to work on Monday.
The toddler played near the pool all afternoon with her cousins.
We wore hats on the cloudy day and walked to the lighthouse.
The bar served salty snacks, cold beer and loud music.

notes: Card top: ',' x11 and ' as' x9 after advice ('go to the ER every time you have a reaction, even if', 'avoid sitting in line with the door as', 'avoid caffeine and nicotine, because'). Output direction promotes because/due/especially/since. Probe weak: 0.08-0.26 on short advice sentences; narrative comma 0.01. Low confidence.
